headlines.text: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures slip as Wall Street reopens from the holiday weekend into a fresh spike in oil prices and inflation jitters.
Brent crude surges toward $97 a barrel as the U.S. and Iran trade fresh strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran threatening a new restricted zone outside the waterway.
Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on roughly $28 billion of U.S. goods -- steel, aluminum, appliances and more -- take effect today, escalating the trade fight.
The Fed's Sept. 16 rate call still hinges on inflation data even after last week's blowout August jobs report showed payrolls smashing forecasts.
Trump ramps up public pressure on the Fed to cut rates, but Chair Kevin Warsh is signaling he may back a hike instead at this month's meeting.
Wall Street braces for Oracle's earnings next week as investors test whether the AI infrastructure trade can keep delivering amid soaring capex.
